tieu_de: Pluto transit through the 6th house: rebuilding the daily grind
mo: Will I lose my job during Pluto in the 6th?
Why do I keep clashing with my manager?
What kind of lifestyle changes suit this transit?

Most of life happens in ordinary hours: the commute, the inbox, the lunch you grab between tasks. That is the territory of the 6th house, and when Pluto moves in, those ordinary hours stop feeling ordinary. Work relationships get charged. Routines that used to hold you together start to feel like a cage.
The most common story of this transit is a workplace struggle. The most useful story is what people build instead: a daily life that actually keeps them well.

doan: The 6th house covers daily work, colleagues, employees, routines, habits and the practical care of your body. P Pluto brings pressure and transformation. In this house, that means your working life and your daily habits are both up for serious change.
At work, Pluto tends to expose power dynamics that were always there. At home, it shows you which habits are quietly wearing you down. Both are invitations to rebuild.
Planet Pluto Rules Scorpio Transformation, rebirth, power

A boss who once seemed fine becomes difficult to work under. A colleague competes for the same project. You find yourself in a standoff, and you notice that you are reacting in exactly the way the other person is: tit for tat, tone for tone. The office starts to feel like a chessboard.
If you manage people, you may deal with a staff member who challenges your authority, or you may realise you have been controlling in ways you did not see.

On the personal side, many people suddenly overhaul their diet, start training seriously, or cut out a habit they have leaned on for years. The body often signals clearly what it needs, and this transit makes it harder to ignore.

This is one of the best periods to transform your lifestyle. Changes to food, sleep, exercise and daily structure made now tend to stick, because they come from a real need rather than a passing resolution.

At work, the transit can lead you to a role or method that fits you far better. People sometimes leave a toxic workplace and find that the next job is healthier in every sense. Others stay and change how they work so the job no longer consumes them.

The danger is escalation. Meeting force with force at work rarely helps and can end with losing a job or a working relationship that mattered. It is easy to get locked into a power struggle and forget what you actually wanted.
There is also a risk of going to extremes with self-improvement: brutal regimes, rigid rules, perfectionism about routines. Pluto prefers deep change over punishing change.

Pluto spends 12 to 30 years in a sign, and a house transit usually lasts on a similar order. Your house system and birth latitude affect the size of the 6th house, so your chapter may be shorter or longer. Themes can return in waves because of Pluto's retrograde periods.
When conflict flares at work, slow down. Write down what you want from the situation before responding. Often the best move is the one the other person does not expect: calm, factual and brief.
Document your work carefully. Clear records protect you when power games start.
Choose one health habit to change properly, get proper guidance where needed, and build from there. Small consistent changes outlast dramatic ones.
Stop tolerating routines that make you miserable just because they are familiar. Start designing a day that includes time for your body, not only your tasks.

Not necessarily. Job changes are common, but many come by choice. The risk rises mainly when power struggles escalate. Keeping your responses measured gives you more control over whether you stay or leave.

Pluto brings hidden power dynamics into the open. The clash may reflect genuine issues in the workplace and also old patterns of how you respond to authority. Looking at both sides gives you more options than simply fighting.
Changes you can sustain for years. Regular movement, better sleep, simpler meals and fewer habits that drain you all fit well. The aim is lasting renewal, not a short burst of discipline.
